[h2]Lust from Beyond: M Edition[/h2]

[h1]....Copy…..Paste….[/h1]

So, I already reviewed the original [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1035120/Lust_from_Beyond/]Lust from Beyond[/url] before. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/UnitedCritics/discussions/0/3033725235503362382/]Here’s the link to that review![/url] I highly recommend reading that review first before coming here. Do not worry, this review will be short as there isn’t a lot of difference between these two games. 

So, why did they release the same game twice? Basically, in some countries, like Germany & China, Adult games are hidden by default. Movie Games Lunarium wanted everyone to get an opportunity to experience their games. Hence, they made a low gore & nudity version of the game just for the players residing in these countries. More information regarding the M Edition can be found [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1641890/view/3115924807146108496]here[/url].

[h1]About This Game [/h1]

I am sure we don’t need this section. Everything you need to know about the game is in my review of the original game. Let me state what’s different here:

[olist]
[*] Nudity and explicit sexual content have been reduced. Example: private parts are now covered by a piece of clothing.
[*] Some scenes have been rearranged to keep their meaning but reduce the explicit factor. Example: an orgy became a ritual cult meeting.
[*] Some animations, scene framing and models have been changed to meet the Mature rating requirements instead of Adult Only.
[/olist]
[i]Source: Lust from Beyond: M Edition FAQ[/i]

If you want the original & full experience and you’re not from those regions where they ban NSFW games, then you should grab the original game. 

[h1]Pros[/h1]
[list]
[*] An interesting plot line.
[*] More varied gameplay when compared to its prequel.
[*] The game has good graphics although most of the things you see are disgusting.
[*] The design & details of the environment are pretty phenomenal.
[…

TAKEN DIRECTLY FROM THE DEVELOPER:

(Q)uestion: Is Lust From Beyond: M Edition a completely new game?
(A)nswer: It is a new version of Lust from Beyond. It’s a game with the same story and gameplay, but with less focus on the explicit content.

Q: Why did you make this version of the game?
A: We’ve put a lot of heart into our game and we wanted to enable more gamers to play it. By default, Adult Only games are unavailable in some markets, like Germany and China. They are also hidden on Steam to everyone unless you manually enable Adult Only titles in your settings.
Besides, Lust from Beyond isn’t gratuitous. Its elements serve to tell the story and invoke certain feelings or thoughts in the players. At heart, it’s a Lovecraftian horror touching upon themes like curiosity, physicality or lust. It’s an immersive story-driven survival horror first, with explicit parts being a cherry on top. It can easily stand on its own without the most extreme elements, so we decided to make it more accessible for the players who look for a more subtle experience.
However, you’ll still find plenty of horror visuals in it!

Q: What is the difference between Lust From Beyond and the M Edition?
A: There are a couple of differences.
Nudity and explicit sexual content have been reduced. Example: private parts are tastefully covered by a piece of clothing (that’s still very much cultish and aligned with the themes of the game).
Some scenes have been rearranged to keep their meaning but reduce the explicit factor. Example: an orgy became a ritual cult meeting.
Some animations, scene framing and models have been changed to meet the Mature rating requirements instead of Adult Only.

Q: What does M stand for?
A: M means the M (Mature) rating, but there’s more to it! At first, we wanted to call it Masked Edition, since we tastefully covered some of the elements of the game. Also, Amanda’s mask is one of the most visually distinct elements of our world. But we went for M, because it’s such an ap…

citations.review_text: I got this as part of a Humble Bundle. While I like the HR Giger aesthetic, overall the technical execution feels a bit subpar. Most of the menus can't be used with a controller. The voice actor recording quality isn't that good. The first missions require opening a bunch of drawers and are very tedious.

Sexy, comfortable with what it is, and some scenes are lit so spectacularly you'd think this is an Unreal Engine game when in reality it was made in Unity.

However, writing seems a bit poor (pulpy, and people playing for the porn are still gonna be pissed) and it felt like the voice director wasn't at the wheel when it came to bringing out the protagonist, who clearly sounds uncomfortable delivering some of the lines, or misinterprets some of the nuance and intent behind them.

Sometime down the road, I'll peck on this some more.

I did receive this game as part of a bundle and didn't purposely seek it out. 

I would not recommend this to anyone.

Completed the first 2 chapters and the only thing I was lusting for, was something to happen.

Boring cupboard searching, handle jiggling (and no, not that kind of handle) simulator that relies of lazy jump scares inbetween edgy erotica.

I got this as part of a Humble Bundle. While I like the HR Giger aesthetic, overall the technical execution feels a bit subpar. Most of the menus can't be used with a controller. The voice actor recording quality isn't that good. The first missions require opening a bunch of drawers and are very tedious.

I really wish I could say something more positive about this game. 
There is something about its atmosphere and art design that I really like, even if it feels a tad too edgy. 
There is something very mysterious going on here that I would love to explore.

But….

The big issue is the gameplay. 
The gameplay is garbage. Even the running and walking mechanics are bad and this is probably the only game I have played, where, if you crouch and look up, you will see what I assume is your own back or the top of your head. This cant be intentional. 

45 minutes in and I arrived at a terrible puzzle. I played it for 45 minutes and I did every single thing I did that brought me closer to solve it out of random luck. There is no sense of logic or good design put into it. You are just thrown into an area without any sense of direction and then you have to pick up items, where each item you pick up, will open up a secret passage to another item. 

This game is not just boring. It is outright frustrating to play.

Lust from Beyond: M Edition is a psychological horror adventure developed by Movie Games Lunarium and published by Movie Games S.A., offering a modified version of the original Lust from Beyond designed to reach a wider audience by removing explicit adult content while preserving the unsettling narrative and disturbing atmosphere. The game blends first-person exploration, puzzle solving, and survival horror elements with heavy inspiration drawn from cosmic horror and dark psychological themes. Set in a world where forbidden rituals and ancient entities lurk beyond human understanding, the experience focuses less on conventional combat and more on narrative immersion, disturbing imagery, and the gradual unraveling of a deeply unsettling mystery.

The story follows Victor Holloway, a man haunted by disturbing visions of a strange and terrifying realm known as Lusst’ghaa. These visions plague his dreams and gradually begin to intrude into his waking life, pushing him toward the edge of sanity. Desperate for answers, Victor begins investigating the origin of these visions and soon becomes entangled with a mysterious cult known as the Church of Ecstasy. What initially appears to be a secretive group dedicated to enlightenment quickly reveals itself to be something far more sinister. As Victor delves deeper into the cult’s rituals and ideology, he uncovers a hidden reality where human desires, ancient gods, and forbidden dimensions intersect in horrifying ways. The narrative slowly reveals that Lusst’ghaa is not simply a hallucination but a tangible dimension inhabited by alien entities that feed on human emotion and obsession.

Gameplay unfolds from a first-person perspective and focuses primarily on exploration and puzzle solving. Players navigate through a variety of environments including Victor’s home, the cult’s mysterious headquarters, underground chambers, and eventually the grotesque otherworldly landscapes of Lusst’ghaa itself. [h1] Lust from Beyond: M Edition [/h1]

[h2] A Toned-Down Horror Still Full of Dread [/h2]
[b]Lust from Beyond: M Edition[/b] strips away the explicit sexual content found in the original release, but the psychological horror and eerie atmosphere remain intact. The game still immerses players in a grotesque world inspired by the works of Lovecraft and Giger, but it treads more carefully when it comes to eroticism, making it more approachable for a broader audience.

[h3] Story and Setting [/h3]
You still take on the role of Victor Halloway, a man plagued by disturbing nightmares that lead him to the creepy town of Bleakmoor. His descent into a world of lust, death, and horror remains unsettling, though the explicit imagery has been toned down. The game's core narrative, driven by a twisted mystery and otherworldly exploration, is just as gripping as ever.

[h3] Atmosphere and Visuals [/h3]
While the erotic elements are censored or removed, [b]M Edition[/b] doesn’t lose the grotesque and nightmarish visuals that define the [b]Lust from Beyond[/b] experience. Lusst’ghaa, the alternate dimension shaped by desire, still feels oppressive and alive. The horror atmosphere, influenced by surreal, organic designs, is enough to provoke fear without relying on graphic content.

[h3] Gameplay and Puzzles [/h3]
The puzzles and exploration are still present, though streamlined. The game follows the same path as the original in this regard, with relatively easy puzzles at first and more challenging ones later. Unfortunately, the inspection mechanic remains underutilized—though it's fun, it doesn’t add much to the overall experience.

[h3] Combat and Enemy Encounters [/h3]
Combat plays out similarly to the original, with an emphasis on survival. You’re encouraged to run and hide rather than fight, and even when armed, the tension from earlier on can disappear once you’re wielding a weapon. Some of the game’s boss encounters stand out, but others feel somewhat underwhelming.

5) VA and Character Work - The Voice acting is fine, shout out to the all star Jonathan who had a voice that matched the mannerisms and was able to pull off…

[b]M Edition[/b]

Let's start with the topic most people are interested in a year after the original version got released. This new edition excludes all genitalia and keeps the nudity to a bare minimum. This means that during orgy scenes all participants have their underwear on. There is one particular scene with defecation - this has completely been removed along with the corresponding achievement that requires us to watch the event play out for several minutes. The gore, violence all remain there essentially not changing the 18+ rating of the game. The world of [i]Lusst'ghaa[/i] has the same design where phallic ornaments and symbols are present. For me this means the atmosphere remains the same - no key element has been removed and the game is enjoyable without the excessive content. I can't tell you why a new game had to be released instead of including two versions under one title - please head for the discussion thread if you're interested in talking about this. 

[b]Between 2 rivaling factions[/b]

We play as Victor, an antiquarian who sets out to visit a doctor due to some nightmares and visions he has. Normally, this wouldn't be a problem but Victor happens to hit his girlfriend after one such nightmare when waking up. Eventually, we find ourselves between two cults that oppose one another: the [i]Cult of Ecstasy[/i] and the [i]Scarlet Lodge[/i]. I reviewed [i]Lust for Darkness[/i] almost 3 years ago which is the predecessor for this game. You don't have to play that to understand what's going on here but I recommend that you play both [i]Prologue[/i] and [i]Scarlet[/i] as they are completely free and they both present us the aforementioned groups.

The story of Victor, the [i]Seeing One[/i], is told in 15 chapters. This is pretty long as it means your first walkthrough can take up to 10 hours. Lovecraft and Giger are strong themes for me, and this game has not disappointed! I absolutely loved the story and the visuals. Especially the alien realm of Lusst'ghaa was stunning, I was taking wallpaper screenhots at every corner.

Only some gameplay mechanics like the combat are somewhat clunky. But that doesn't deter much from the overall unique atmosphere. I didn't have the feeling that the censored version has mitigated my experience - actually I am glad they made this version, because otherwise I wouldn't have been able to play this game at all in my country.

All in all definitely a recommendation! I hope they do another game with a similar setting in the future!

The game is really great. The devs made a detailed and interesting world which tells its story without just lore dumping you in form of letters, books and diaries. Really good in terms of show not tell. The atmosphere is creepy and it's fun to go and explore the scenes. The visuals are fantastic, even on lower settings (see below). The story and storytelling is really the strong suite here. It feels like every choice was made to enhance that experience. 

The reuse of scenes is well executed. You often return to the same locations but every time you can access different areas which makes it fun to explore every time. It also gives you the opportunity to collect everything you missed the last time.

+ story and storytelling, from start to finish
+ atmosphere
+ music, sound, voice acting!!
+ graphics
+ feels fair (solvable puzzles, easy combat and sneaking)
+ few well placed jump scares

I was captivated by the game's creepy atmosphere, interesting art direction, and excellent locations. The plot is very engaging, and the characters we meet on our way are terrifying. I strongly recommend it to every horror fan.

it everything else that is the problem, 

this game is pretty much like outlast except we have to drag our mouse to open doors, everything feel so slow in term of movement and characters, the A.I enemy feel so dumb that you can run around in circle and then hide thus making them actually forgot where we at

Thank you! [/quote]

This is a survival horror game with a gripping storyline, interesting puzzles, dark occult atmosphere, incredible game design, and very stupid AI. The fast-paced action scenes look great while the game design and soundtrack are excellent, so due to this, you can fully immerse yourself in its atmosphere. The game world is thoroughly designed, and the exploration of it will allow you to discover many dark secrets. The main disadvantage however, is the stupid AI. Said stupid AI is especially noticeable in open areas since you can simply run around the enemy by turning a meter away from them. Also in this game you often have to make decisions quickly, while the decision itself isn't always obvious. Lastly the duration of loading screens in the game after death takes way more time than they should, which spoils the overall impression of the game. A generally good game, but its issues leave a bad taste in your mouth.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the game lacks a chapter selection or manual save system, making it difficult to replay specific sections or recover missed items without starting over.

citations.review_text:
I really loved this game, was awesome. Got me scared a few times and the story was more than decent, but the game has 2 big minuses.

- No chapter menu selection, so you cannot replay a chapter. If you miss something start the game from zero.
- No restart chapter. There is a restart button but it will restart you at the last autosave checkpoint which mean zero.

But besides these  two big minuses, still recommend the game, is very nice.

I'm enjoying this game a lot more than the last one. The story is a little interesting. I enjoy the puzzles a lot more too. My main criticism is that there is no manual save so we could go back to a certain chapter (though I haven't finished the game so there might be). Also, I enjoy exploring though it makes it a little hard with a big fat dude chasing you and the game tells you that you can't defeat.

I avoided buying this game for quite some time because it looked like a porn game and the title of the game sure didn’t help either. While I don’t mind games with sex I didn’t want a game that focused on it. After seeing this game repeatedly recommended I decided to finally buy it and see what it was about.

I will say this….it is not a porn game, it’s main focus is a horror game but it does have a whole lot of sexual themes, and there are a few sex scenes (I think 5) that happen throughout the game.

The story of the game was really good. You were having extreme visions and you sought out help. You ended up being kidnapped by one cult and then saved by another. You are shown how the visions are actually a real place where you need to uncover the reason and truth to them. 

Everything in the game was well done from the voice acting to the graphics and the environment. The gameplay was pretty basic where you would hide if you encountered an enemy or engage battle if you had weapons. The puzzles weren’t too hard and were engaging enough to feel satisfied when completed. 

There were some annoyances where the game would glitch and you would have to restart the check point. Being noticed and trying to lose the enemy felt impossible so it was better to die usually. There’s also no save slots or cloud saving so that was very inconvenient when I wanted to play on my pc and then play on the steam deck. The game has some performance issues on the deck related to the shadows and anything set higher than low would hit the performance so bad it would tank the frame rate to 20fps. Keeping shadows on low would keep the game at 60fps most of the game.

I rather enjoyed this game tho and am glad I decided to play it rather than ignore it.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as clunky and unpolished, with some stating the game would be better without it.

citations.review_text:
Lovecraft and Giger are strong themes for me, and this game has not disappointed! I absolutely loved the story and the visuals. Especially the alien realm of Lusst'ghaa was stunning, I was taking wallpaper screenhots at every corner.

Only some gameplay mechanics like the combat are somewhat clunky. But that doesn't deter much from the overall unique atmosphere. I didn't have the feeling that the censored version has mitigated my experience - actually I am glad they made this version, because otherwise I wouldn't have been able to play this game at all in my country.

All in all definitely a recommendation! I hope they do another game with a similar setting in the future!

The puzzles are fun but the combat is awful. The controls are so frustrating and do not respond, which is aggravating when you are being attacked. I can't press the buttons any more than I am already pressing them. It reloads at inconvenient spots, without healing you, and makes you redo tedious, repetitive tasks. If I have to skip past the same two cut scenes, grab the key to free myself, pick up the gun and the rest of my items (pliers, ammo. 2 picture frames, health box, knife, and 4 different knick-knacks) from that stupid chest just to die again, I'm going to self-destruct. 
There is also a boss who is glitched. I spent hours fighting and re-fighting TIm. I got GREAT at it by the end. Tim couldn't land a hit, and I was filling him full of bullets--but Tim would not die. P.S. Tim is a stupid name for a Leather Daddy.

A most excellent tale of cosmic horror, dread, sex, lies and beauty. This game is a gem beyond words in some regards. It's not without its flaws such somewhat janky combat, and the odd bug. But overall, the positives far outweighed the negatives.

To sum it up in a few words: Beautiful, strange, terrifying, and intriguing. Definitely a must-play for lovers of Cosmic Horror.

TL;DR - Get the Base version, not the M Edition. There are some improvements over Lust For Darkness, but this plays closer to the Bethesda Call of Cthulhu game. Worldbuilding, Lore, and Environment textures are pretty good. Script is wack, but the story is good. Voice Acting was fine, voice direction needs work. 


Tentatively Recommending It - If you liked the Bethesda Call of Cthulhu Game, you will probably enjoy it. 

I played this after playing the first game, Lust for Darkness. So I've got a relatively thought out idea on this.

1) I will say don't bother with M Edition, just buy the original. This is sexy lovecraft with cults and orgies and ♥♥♥♥. You shouldn't really have a dip your toe in approach to it. I feel like I missed a lot of what I was signing up for which was messed up weird sexy stuff, and while this delivered some, it was clearly hamstrung from the original cut. 

2) There has been a big texture upgrade and I am here for it. The worldbuilding and the lore in this game is pretty good and being able to appreciate fabrics, surfaces, and just general textures helps lean you into the fact that this game is sensory-oriented.  That is really good. 

3) Modeling and Textures - The Models are better than the first game, though they still leave a lot to be desired.

4) Combat System - This is a net negative across the board. I did not find one scene with combat to be interesting or satisfying it. I would have rather kept the get spotted get ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rekt approach like the first game did. Easily the BIGGEST drawback of this is the fact that if you take one damage, you permanently have red haze vision and this is incredibly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying because up until the last 1/3rd of the game you will seldom find healing items. It really just gets in the way of the detective work and gets in the way of the story. 

5) VA and Character Work - The Voice acting is fine, shout out to the all star Jonathan who had a voice that matched the mannerisms and was able to pull off…

First of all I wanna say this isn't a bad game. I played all the other "Lust" games before except the uncensored version of Lust From Beyond. I only played the M Edition instead because it was way cheaper for me and the uncut version isn't available in my country (Germany). How I love that...
So I haven't exactly the comparison but as I played the other "Lust" games I can imagine; also it's often pretty obvious when something got censored in the M Edition. And I must say the censoring in this game usually feels pretty cheap. Especially in a game which is all about Lust and Sex. It's like playing a shooter but all guns or blood is censored.
This isn't my main complaint with the game tho, other points are:
-performance can often be quite poor which isn't a big deal tho as the game is mostly a walking sim...
-speaking of the genre: the game also tries out some combat which is implemented quite bad, the game would be better without it; don't believe the store page saying this game is a survival horror game. There is like one part of a level which actually feels like survial horror, the rest is (horror) walking sim with puzzles here and there
-the game is too long for it's own good; especially since you have to do a lot of tedious tasks, also there is just too much dialog in it. If you would cut all the dialogs, the cutscenes and the tedious stuff, there is sadly not much left.
-story and gameplay contradicts themself quite often: like some guys want to capture you alive, but if they happen to get to you in gameplay, they try to kill you

Honestly I feel like the game wouldn't be great if it wouldn't be censored (i.e. the og Lust From Beyond). I mean no game from these devs is, but I would probably rate it positive even tho not by much. But the censored version feels kinda pointless to me.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience long loading times throughout the game, particularly after death and when transitioning between areas.

citations.review_text:
The plot and the universe are really good, some UX details are very good.

But I was disappointed by the fact that you can't go back on your choices.
If you are playing of a HDD, the loading time between scenes will be long.

Not a bad game. The long loading times is probably the biggest flaw this game has.
Besides that there are a few things that I didn't like but most of it is good and the story was interesting although predictable.

So a relatively simple story with some plot twists, a lot of "shock" events/scenes, an ok cast of characters and some puzzle/stealth/combat elements.

In what universe does "M-version" mean censored? I accidentally bought the censored version, didn't try it out until a month later and that means I can't get a refund on it.

This game also has some serious loading issues. It's not the first time I've had issues with it. When I first bought it last year it wouldn't start at all. It was a common bug and I couldn't get any help from customer support. Now with a new computer it does work. It's just completely pointless. This game isn't that good to begin with. You're mostly just walking around, gathering stuff to put in the mail. Oh, but there's one riveting quest where you have to go back to your car to get a coin for a pay phone.

Got for free in the Ukraine humble bundle, played about a third of the game before I couldn't be bothered anymore. The story may get better later on but frankly wasn't that interesting up to the start of chapter 5. As many other people have said the game is terribly optimised, with a buttery smooth 30 FPS at medium graphics (my computer isn't the best but isn't terrible). The graphics are alright at higher settings but as I said terribly optimised, but at lower settings could have come out a decade ago. The loading times are also horrendous for what it is. At one point I pulled out a timer and found that it took nearly 2 minutes to load the relatively small area town area in chapter 3. Many of these criticisms I understand are completely unavoidable with a small team working on this game.

My much larger criticisms come from other aspects of the game. "Gameplay"wise, as many others said, the game mostly boils down to a walking sim but to be fair, it also involves a lot of searching. A good way of thinking about it is that it takes the searching and using items style of puzzle (if that's what it should be called) in games like amnesia but not being able to use the same recipe to make this style succeed. I'm not an expert in game design (obviously), but I would guess that it is something to do with a lack of threat in the environment and tension that a game like amnesia would use to make the walking from place to place to get items more interesting as opposed to just glorified fetch quests. Combat was a joke from what I saw; the enemies all move slower than you, so if you can avoid getting cornered you can basically just keep running past them. Voice acting was borderline emotionless and by mid way through chapter 2 I was already just reading the subs and mashing space. The environments in the dream (or whatever it was) were cool but felt lacking in some way, resulting in it making me feel like oh ok I guess this is a new place for me to walk through.

My single bigge…

Yeah dude that was one hell of an experience

I don't even know how to describe it. Weird mix of SCORN, Resident Evil 7, the Amnesia series, Layers of Fear, and plenty of stuff that gives the game its name. It's worth noting that there are three games before this. Lust for Darkness, Lust from Beyond: Prologue, and Lust from Beyond: Scarlet, and they're all just as messed up as this, perhaps moreso given that this is the "M Edition" which is as opposed to the regular, Adult-Only version.

Absolutely not for the faint of heart, this has some ballsy subject matter. I will say I think some people may get motion sickness? There's this weird issue where if you walk onto a slope, the camera shifts without mouse movement, and there is a lot of janky collision that gets walked on. It's kinda crazy that something this severe made it through the production of four whole games, because everything else is remarkably well-done for an indie company I've otherwise never heard of.

The camera pans upward and spins i do love what i have played so far tho difficult it was i had to exit and restart a lot just to get through the camera i tried different sensitivety settings on the mouse and even hooked up a controller but it didn't stop the camera it is frustrating and i play games to get rid of frustration not be more frustrated because a camera makes me pick up my mouse every 2 seconds to reset the physical position of my mouse as i am constantly going off the edge of my desk trying to keep the camera in a way that i can see what is happening and because of this i die more than i should as i can't see what is in front of me i love the way the game looks i love the stories in it that i have seen so far  but the camera kills it for me I did give it a thumbs down initually for the camera but have since changed my mind and gave it a thumbs because i do love the game so far it is a great game except for the one issue and i can't give a bad review based on a camera

It's also very bad optimized and GPU is going crazy (RTX 3070 ti)

TL;DR Very good story based game with fantastic sound design and atmosphere. Some minor bugs but nothing that would make it unplayable. Get it if you want a cool cult Lovecraftian story game.

The game is really great. The devs made a detailed and interesting world which tells its story without just lore dumping you in form of letters, books and diaries. Really good in terms of show not tell. The atmosphere is creepy and it's fun to go and explore the scenes. The visuals are fantastic, even on lower settings (see below). The story and storytelling is really the strong suite here. It feels like every choice was made to enhance that experience. 

The reuse of scenes is well executed. You often return to the same locations but every time you can access different areas which makes it fun to explore every time. It also gives you the opportunity to collect everything you missed the last time.

So plus points are (not ranked):
+ story and storytelling, from start to finish
+ atmosphere
+ music, sound, voice acting!!
+ graphics
+ feels fair (solvable puzzles, easy combat and sneaking)
+ few well placed jump scares

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the title of the 'M Edition' is misleading, as they mistakenly believed 'M' stood for mature or uncensored adult content rather than censored.

citations.review_text:
I had to stop because ultimately the mechanics of this game are horrendous. 
Enemies see you through walls and sometimes can walk through the object you are hiding behind to hunt you. 

Interesting horror storyline. But couldn't get past the clunky. 
I had assumed M meant explicit content, but it actually means censored. 

I played through a significant part of the story before giving up and looking up. Learned what the original version was, anyone who thinks this version is not VERY different is incorrect. First and foremost the original undertone of the game for this version did not hint at how terrible of a human being we are, I had just assumed we were a good human with a bad habit... that be incorrect... Which not knowing how that first Chapter originally was written really changes the entire dynamic of the game. (SA)

Should have done my homework to know that this version is a heavily censored one. Funny it's called edition Mature. Had to watch videos of the original version to see the big difference. Though I understand that making a version like this can introduce the game to more audience especially in restricted regions, I would have spent more efforts to get access to the original one had I known the difference. It would have been a completely different experience.

BEWARE: THIS "M EDITION" IS THE CENSURED ONE.
I do not see any other reasons to label it if not to scam customers.
Do not buy this version, the mature part is an essential one to the game.

So I had seen this game before and had thought about trying it and then it came up in part of a bundle. I was aware there was the original game and then a censored version, as far as I was concerned it would only be worth playing the original uncensored version, so when this version said this was the M version (ie I assumed like most would that this was the MATURE version) I bought the bundle only to discover for some bizarre reason M meant NOT Mature ie censored. I have played a fair bit of it and it's OK but | dislike the timed elements for example in the theatre when you have to complete the tasks in a set order within a time limit and as far as I could work out it took several attempts until you worked out what to do so leading to multiple deaths until I'd sussed it out. Simply because I think the title is misleading I don't recommend it.

In what universe does "M-version" mean censored? I accidentally bought the censored version, didn't try it out until a month later and that means I can't get a refund on it.
